races.name: Personal Touches Day Of Elegance Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Empire Rising
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field; a recent Thirsk winner over 8f on good going gives her a course-and-distance edge, and Darragh Keenan can set a controlled gallop to maximise her chance — her similar-going record is modest but her role here is to control, not to finish fastest.|
runners_data.comment: Empire Rising arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience over today's trip, making him a clear danger here; the main risk is that four of his last five starts have yielded only that single victory, so consistency remains the question.

runners_data.name: Love Tanya
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners a filly whose form reads 2-2-3 in three starts, all on good ground over 6f-7f; stepping up to a flat mile on good-to-soft should suit her stamina profile and Bethell's yard is in reasonable form at 3/22 over 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, Love Tanya has finished second, second, and third in her last three outings and has run over today's trip, making her the one to keep on side. She carries 134 lb from stall one and, although yet to score, her rating of 84 marks her as the class act here.

runners_data.name: The Monkey King
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's colt won his last start over 7f on good ground and will likely slot in just behind the leader; the trainer's 8/42 14-day strike rate is strong and Rhys Clutterbuck keeps the ride, suggesting connections are confident about stepping up to a mile.|
runners_data.comment: Returned to winning ways last time out, though he was sixth three starts back and only third two starts back suggests some inconsistency; has run over today's trip and comes here fit enough on 30 days' rest, but his official rating of 72 leaves little room for error from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Coco Nova
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (just two starts) and carries the unknown-quantity caveat, but both runs have been on good ground and Hugo Palmer's yard is ticking along; style listed as unknown so positional flexibility is a genuine asset if she travels well.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts, Coco Nova ranks seventh of nine on our figures and looks hard to fancy at the weights, carrying 131 lb from stall six; a third last time out and experience over today's trip offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Akaraka
runners_data.note: Three starts all on good ground, all at shorter distances (6f-7f), and the form figures of 7-8-7 make encouraging hard to find; Michael Bell's 3/18 14-day return is fair but this filly has yet to show she warrants market support.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and beaten some way on each occasion, Akaraka at least has experience over today's trip and arrives freshened after 40 days off, with our rating suggesting he holds more ability than his official mark of 70 implies — the worry is his recent form offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Or Another
runners_data.note: Smart recent form over sprint trips (three placings in five), but this is a genuine hold-up horse pushed forward on the map simply because the rear of the field is overcrowded — over a mile on soft ground with a modest pace, the trip and likely race shape both work against her.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, Or Another arrives here on a quick nine-day turnaround with a third two runs back offering some encouragement, though a seventh three starts back and 130 lb to carry are the challenges he must overcome.

runners_data.name: Prince Kameo
runners_data.note: Won his latest start over 8f on standard Wolverhampton ground, so the step to a flat mile is no issue; a true hold-up type under Kevin Stott, he needs the pace to be honest enough to set up a late run, which is not guaranteed under Empire Rising's likely control.|
runners_data.comment: Prince Kameo won last time out and returns on a quick nine-day turnaround with a trainer striking at 35%, but ranked eighth of nine on our figures and carrying 130 lb, he looks up against it despite having run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Sou'wester
runners_data.note: A filly whose form reads 5-5-5 across three starts including a soft-ground run; she is a natural hold-up horse placed in midfield on the map only because the rear is saturated — Tim Easterby is a prolific trainer but 86 days off is a significant query.|
runners_data.comment: Sou'wester has run over today's trip and going and our rating puts him as a leading threat in this field, yet he arrives 86 days since his last start and has been winless in his last three runs, so the key question is whether he returns to form sharply enough here.

runners_data.name: Northern Viola
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 55 and a hold-up horse by nature, shifted forward on the map for logistical reasons rather than tactical ones; three consecutive fifth and seventh placings at shorter trips give no reason to think a mile on soft ground resolves matters.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Northern Viola also returns from a 64-day absence, making her hard to fancy; she has run over today's trip before and carries 116 lb from stall eight.

races.paceDynamic: Empire Rising is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on this flat Thirsk mile on good-to-soft ground, she is expected to stride to the front unchallenged and dictate at a sustainable, controlled tempo. With no genuine rival willing or able to dispute the lead, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which historically at Thirsk favours horses who can travel prominently and pick up rather than those who need a true test of stamina from deep in the field. The Monkey King is the most natural prominent chaser and could sit a close second, while Love Tanya, Coco Nova, and Prince Kameo are capable of tracking the pace from mid-division. Crucially, Or Another, Sou'wester, and Northern Viola are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because the rear is over-populated; their true racing patterns are further back, meaning they face an additional challenge if the pace is modest. This race shape decisively favours prominent and lead-tracking profiles — horses who can sit within striking range of Empire Rising early and deploy their finishing effort with control, rather than closers who need a searching gallop to generate the momentum they require from far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Empire Rising bowls along uncontested at a fair-to-moderate pace with The Monkey King and Love Tanya tracking through the early stages.
scenarios.body: Empire Rising dictates every yard, sets a comfortable fractions that keeps the held-up horses anchored at the rear with little time to reel her in over the final two furlongs; the prominent duo who travel well within themselves emerge as the chief dangers in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Empire Rising's lead is measured rather than overly comfortable and the tracking pair build momentum from the home turn.
scenarios.body: The Monkey King or Love Tanya, sitting a length or two off the leader into the final quarter-mile, produce a sustained challenge that the front runner cannot repel on softening ground; ground that tests stamina lightly suits these stepping-up travellers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Surprise Closer Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace develops enough genuine tempo — perhaps Coco Nova or Prince Kameo pushing forward — to create a genuine finish from further back.
scenarios.body: A truer gallop stretches the field and allows a hold-up horse with reserves to pick up ground through the final furlong; Prince Kameo, most recently a winner over this trip on standard ground, is best positioned among the rear group to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Collapse Muddle
scenarios.trigger: If Empire Rising's tactics backfire — either she goes too fast early for soft ground or is shuffled back — causing a messy, stop-start race shape.
scenarios.body: Confusion in the early stages disrupts expected positions, opening a window for a fortunate closer to emerge from the chaos, though the redistributed hold-up types would still need an exceptional run to benefit meaningfully.

watchPoints.text: Empire Rising's early pace — if she is allowed to stride clear unchallenged through the first half-mile, prominent stalkers The Monkey King and Love Tanya are the chief dangers, but a collapse in her gallop before the turn could open the race to any finisher.|

The Monkey King's jockey Rhys Clutterbuck must decide immediately whether to press up to track Empire Rising or settle further back; if he is caught in no-man's-land between the leader and the midfield pack, he could be outpaced when the race quickens.|

Or Another, Sou'wester, and Northern Viola are all genuine closers mapped forward on the diagram artificially — if the tempo does not genuinely test stamina over this mile, all three face a near-impossible task converting their natural style into a winning position.|

The going is officially good-to-soft at this race's time per the going report — softer than many of these runners' best form, and Empire Rising's one run on soft (11th of 6f) is a mild flag if the ground deteriorates further through the card.|

Prince Kameo ran just nine days ago and won; monitor for any freshness concerns or jockey instructions from Kevin Stott that suggest connections are managing the horse rather than expecting a peak effort second time out in quick succession.|

races.name: Jw4x4 Northallerton Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Roots In Touche
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over 5f Good and finished second over the same trip on soft, giving genuine confidence in style and going suitability, but OR 77 and hood worn suggests needs things to fall perfectly; faces a direct fight for the lead with Black Velvet Boy.|
runners_data.comment: Winner one start back, and she has experience of today's trip and going to call on — Roots In Touche carries 129 lb from stall seven but our rating of 90 just edges her ahead of her rivals, making her the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Casino Star
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's hold-up juvenile has strong soft-ground form (2/5f/SOF) and a fine recent record of placing at this trip, and Pierre-Louis Jamin is an astute judge of pace; benefits directly if the front-runners soften each other up.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Casino Star has been placed three times in that span but also beaten out of the frame on other occasions, making him hard to fancy ranked eighth of nine on our figures; he does at least return after just 16 days and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Concert Pitch
runners_data.note: Has been placing repeatedly over 5f including a soft-ground second, and Connor Beasley will place him handy off the contested pace; the question is whether he has the finishing kick to convert all those seconds into a win.|
runners_data.comment: Concert Pitch arrives on the back of a win last time out and has shown consistent placing in recent starts, with seconds two, three and four starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and going; however, a trainer strike-rate of just 5% over the past fortnight is a notable dampener.

runners_data.name: This Moment
runners_data.note: George Boughey's prominent racer tops the weights at OR 83 and has a Tapeta win on record, but all five recent runs listed are on Good or Tapeta surfaces with no soft-ground turf evidence — going suitability is the key unknown.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures and saddled by a trainer firing at just four per cent over the past fortnight, This Moment is hard to fancy despite a win last time out; he has run over today's trip and carries 135 lb from stall three.

runners_data.name: Black Velvet Boy
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 5f Good make him the most in-form runner in the field, and Jason Hart will ensure he gets his pitch at the front; the contest for the lead with Roots In Touche is the central tactical question — if he dominates it cleanly, he remains a serious threat even in soft conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Black Velvet Boy arrives on the back of back-to-back wins, though a third three starts back and a seventh four starts back temper expectations a touch; he has run over today's trip and steps up 19 days fresh, but 132 lb from stall 8 is no small ask.

runners_data.name: Furturra
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's prominent runner has a soft-going run (13th/6f/SOF) that is uninspiring, and only 9 days since last run may indicate the stable are confident, but the step back from 6f to 5f and the soft ground are genuine queries.|
runners_data.comment: Furturra catches the eye on fitness, returning just nine days after his last start, and his experience over today's trip and going gives him every right to feature; from stall two carrying 129 lb, the concern is a run of five starts without a win.

runners_data.name: Princesse d'Orange
runners_data.note: Won on soft over 5f (1/5f/SOF) so the going is not a concern, and David O'Meara's stable is in decent form (T14: 7/48), but she has been well beaten in her last two and 38 days off will need to be managed.|
runners_data.comment: Princesse d'Orange caught the eye with a win in her last five starts and arrives fit enough on 38 days since her last run, with experience over today's trip and going; the concern is her two most recent outings have been disappointing, including a ninth last time out.

runners_data.name: Savage Mariner
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish and runs in a hood, which combined with a form string of 2000 and recent heavy defeats (16th, 11th) paints a concerning picture; Hugo Palmer has only 3/27 in 14 days and there is little here to suggest a revival.|
runners_data.comment: Savage Mariner ran second four starts back and arrives here with experience over today's trip, a solid weight-carrier at 135 lb from stall one, and a rating of 86 suggesting he retains ability — the concern is three unplaced efforts in his last three outings leave him winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Anchiano
runners_data.note: Won over 5f Good and placed at the trip for George Scott, and 44 days off is the primary concern, but if fit and forward he has the profile to come from hold-up into a race softened by the pace duel; Darragh Keenan is capable at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Anchiano won two starts back and placed since, and our rating of 70 ranks him last of nine here, making him hard to fancy despite the distance experience and a placed effort 44 days ago.

races.paceDynamic: Black Velvet Boy and Roots In Touche are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the outset over this flat 5f at Thirsk on Good To Soft ground, creating a genuinely contested early pace rather than a soft, uncontested gallop. This pace battle is further complicated by Concert Pitch, This Moment, Furturra, and Princesse d'Orange all wanting prominent positions, meaning four of nine runners will be scrapping for the first two or three spots inside the opening furlong — a recipe for traffic and positional friction 2-3 furlongs out as the pace group concertinas. The contested nature of the lead should ensure the early fractions are honest rather than crawling, which on soft ground will extract a genuine stamina toll on those burning fuel up front. This race shape most favours hold-up horses and late finishers with genuine soft-ground credentials, as the pace war will leave a gap for closers to exploit in the final furlong — though the field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all achieve their ideal berth, with Black Velvet Boy (stronger recent form, 1-1 in last two) most likely to actually secure the lead over Roots In Touche.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Black Velvet Boy and Roots In Touche fight for the lead and set a testing gallop that softens the prominent group.
scenarios.body: The contested early pace drains the front-runners and prominent horses in the soft ground, leaving the closers with a clear advantage entering the final furlong as the leaders tie up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel is moderate rather than brutal and one prominent tracker sits close enough to pounce without being burned.
scenarios.body: A prominent runner positioned second or third settles just off the contested lead and has enough left to outfinish the tiring pace-setters; soft ground suits those who travel economically within a group rather than those leading or chasing hard.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Grinds Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lead pair secures a clear advantage early and the pace is not as searingly contested as feared.
scenarios.body: Black Velvet Boy, on the back of back-to-back wins, could dictate a controlled gallop and prove hard to reel in on 5f where there is no time to recover; this scenario requires Roots In Touche to capitulate quickly in the battle for supremacy.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Left Too Much To Do
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly moderate and prominent types get a soft lead, leaving hold-up horses with insufficient time to close over only 5f.
scenarios.body: In a 5f sprint on a flat track, even soft ground rarely creates enough pace collapse to allow pure hold-up horses to motor through from the back if the early splits are steady; Casino Star and Savage Mariner would find themselves finishing into beaten horses.

watchPoints.text: Black Velvet Boy and Roots In Touche — if either edges the lead battle decisively in the first furlong, the losing front-runner will bleed energy for the rest of the 5f and the pace shape changes entirely.

Concert Pitch, This Moment, Furturra, and Princesse d'Orange — four prominent runners cannot all get their preferred second or third slot; whoever gets squeezed or has to check entering the first furlong could be beaten before the race begins.
Anchiano — 44 days off for George Scott's runner means fitness is unproven; if sharp, the hold-up profile suits the scenario, but a backward showing would be a red flag for future reference.

Savage Mariner — hood and a fading-in-finish flag with four consecutive poor efforts means watch how he travels in the early stages; any sign of reluctance or dropping back immediately would confirm the trend rather than reverse it.

Going confirmation listed as Good To Soft throughout Thirsk's card — softer than the headline SOFT description, which may reduce the stamina advantage for pure hold-up types and keep the race slightly more open for prominent runners than the pace dynamic alone suggests.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Restricted Novice Stakes (for Horses In Bands B, C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ma Blushin Rosie
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with recent soft-ground form (placed 3rd over 6f on Soft), giving her a meaningful going advantage here; Adrian Keatley trainer, 17 days since last run, and her one similar-going start was a placing — well placed to track Uncle Zello's pace.

runners_data.name: Scottys Rocket
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's hold-up filly has run on Good ground over 5f; her two runs show she operates best off a strong pace, which this modest gallop may not provide — going is fine but race shape is the concern.

runners_data.name: Texting
runners_data.note: Hold-up style on record over 7f and 6f on Good and Standard; this trip looks suitable but she will need the pace to genuinely collapse on Good to Soft to get competitive from her natural rear position.

runners_data.name: Voyager One
runners_data.note: Michael Bell-trained hold-up type who has only run over 8f on Good; stepping down in trip and up in ground simultaneously makes this a significant unknown, and her style puts her at a tactical disadvantage if Uncle Zello sets an easy lead.

runners_data.name: Malulee
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish; ran 11th over 5f on Good last time, and with 39 days off and a tendency to weaken, soft ground over 6f compounds the concern — very hard to recommend from a pace-fit perspective.

runners_data.name: Uncle Zello
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here, though tagged [STYLE_FIT=0.93] indicating he is technically racing slightly out of role; his 3rd over 6f Good and 11th over 7f Standard suggest he will lead but may not be the one to beat when it matters — more a pace-setter than a winner.

runners_data.name: Lord Bishop
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison debutant with no public form; unknown style and lightly raced flag apply, but Ellison's 2/21 in the 14-day window and the stable's awareness of Lord Bishop's readiness make this horse worth monitoring as a potential dark horse.

runners_data.name: Callisterra
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' prominent type has a solid recent profile: 2nd and 3rd over 6f on Good and a 5th over 5f — consistent form at this trip and Connor Beasley takes the ride; her prominent style is ideally matched to the predicted race shape.

runners_data.name: Hair Raising
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's runner is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural rear position is unachievable in this crowded field, forcing a midfield slot — the race shape with Uncle Zello's unchallenged lead works against her true style, even if her 3rd over 5f on Good shows ability.

runners_data.name: Dontlookanyfurther
runners_data.note: John & Sean Quinn's runner is a prominent type who won over 6f on Good last time (form: 1); 14 days between runs and top weight of 134lbs are notable negatives, but positional profile suits this pace scenario well.

runners_data.name: Pippy Boy
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish debutant — no public form and unknown style; the yard is 1/12 in the 14-day window which is modest, and without a known running position or going profile this runner is genuinely opaque.

runners_data.name: Rum Point
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll sends out this debutant with no prior form; unknown style flag applies and the trainer's 2/10 recent record offers a small clue the yard sends runners ready — but the racing position will only become clear at the start.

runners_data.name: Reddy
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's runner placed 3rd over 6f on Standard last time and is lightly raced; unknown style flag but going is listed as OK — 10 days since last run and a yard with 4/33 in 14 days suggests she arrives in decent form, though Standard-to-Soft ground switch is worth noting.

races.paceDynamic: Uncle Zello is the one confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, with no significant challenger disputing the lead, he is expected to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on the Good to Soft ground at Thirsk's flat 6f. Ma Blushin Rosie, Callisterra, and Dontlookanyfurther will press forward from the prominent positions, creating a competitive but not frantic early tempo that is unlikely to be truly searching on this surface. The bulk of the field — Scottys Rocket, Texting, Voyager One, Hair Raising, and Malulee — are genuine hold-up or midfield types who will need the pace to collapse late, but with Uncle Zello setting an unchallenged rhythm that rate is unlikely to become punishing enough to bring all of them home. Hair Raising, a true hold-up horse redistributed to mapped midfield because the rear is overcrowded with hold-up types, cannot rely on getting its natural deep position, further compromising its chance. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape favours prominent racers who can track the steady lead and pick it up in the final two furlongs, rather than genuine closers who need a truly honest gallop to close the gap.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Uncle Zello controls a sustainable gallop and the hold-up horses fail to generate sufficient momentum off a modest pace.
scenarios.body: Uncle Zello dictates from the front with Ma Blushin Rosie and Callisterra tracking closely, and the race resolves in the final furlong as those prominent types use their positional advantage on ground that rewards those travelling smoothly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutants Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of the lightly-raced unknown horses (Lord Bishop, Pippy Boy, Rum Point) shows superior raw ability on debut and outruns their inexperience.
scenarios.body: An unknown with unexposed ability tracks the pace handily and, unencumbered by prior limitations, finds a decisive turn of foot in the final furlong that experienced runners cannot match.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves stronger than expected, burning out the prominent horses and allowing genuine hold-up types to come home fast.
scenarios.body: Scottys Rocket or Voyager One would need to be produced very late with a sustained run, benefiting from any fade in the front group, though the modest pace makes this scenario materially less likely given their redistributed or natural rear positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Uncle Zello goes too hard early relative to conditions and the whole field tightens up in a scramble home.
scenarios.body: A compressed finish in the final furlong would bring all styles into play, but horses with a strong finishing kick and clean passage — likely those just off the pace — would benefit most from the resulting tactical lottery.

watchPoints.text: Uncle Zello must be tracked from the break — if he is seriously challenged for the lead by Ma Blushin Rosie or Dontlookanyfurther the pace could spike sharply, reshaping the entire tactical picture and opening the door for hold-up horses.

Malulee's tendency to fade in the finish combined with 39 days off and soft ground over 6f creates a welfare and interference risk if she weakens sharply into the path of hold-up horses coming from behind in the final two furlongs.

Hair Raising cannot be expected to get her natural deep position in a 13-runner field with this many hold-up types; James Sullivan's positioning decision in the first furlong will be critical — if she is stuck wide and deep she is running at a structural disadvantage.

The three debutants — Lord Bishop, Pippy Boy, and Rum Point — are entirely unknown quantities in terms of breaking habits and early positioning; a poor break from any of them in a field of 13 on soft ground could cause significant interference in the early stages.

Dontlookanyfurther carries top weight at 134lbs, a significant burden on Good to Soft ground in a novice field; watch whether Jason Hart rides him handy or drops him in, as his weight-carrying ability over 6f soft will be tested against his prominent profile.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Oolong Poobong
runners_data.note: Clear pace advantage in this field with a likely uncontested lead; Bethell has three winners from 22 runners in the last 14 days and Beasley knows this horse well, but her sole win on soft came over 7f in a small sample and her STYLE_FIT tag means any disruption to her lead role sharply dents her chance.
runners_data.comment: Oolong Poobong shaped with promise when third last time out, returning here in good order after just 16 days, and she has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the concern is whether she can rediscover the form that saw her a winner five starts back, with 140 lb to shoulder today.

runners_data.name: Figjam
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's hold-up filly has placed twice in eleven starts on similar ground and this good-to-soft 7f at Thirsk plays to her genuine closer profile — she doesn't need to be involved early, just needs the pace to be real enough to reel in front-runners late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Figjam nonetheless rates the one to beat on our figures, and having run over today's trip and going she has no excuses on conditions, with a 16-day turnaround leaving her fit enough to go close from stall four.

runners_data.name: Perfect Part
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason takes over on Brian Ellison's hold-up mare who placed second over 8f on good-to-soft and has shown she stays well; the switch back to 7f from longer trips is a question, and she has yet to convert a placed run into a win in fifteen similar-going starts.
runners_data.comment: Perfect Part shaped with promise when second four starts back and arrives on the back of a 16-day break in solid enough condition, with experience over today's trip and going lending her claims; the concern is a trainer firing at just 5% in the past fortnight, and she remains winless in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Passing Thought
runners_data.note: Ed Walker has seven winners from 37 runners in the past fortnight, and this three-year-old owns a win on soft and a win on good-to-soft over 6-7f — her prominent style could see her slot in behind Oolong Poobong naturally, and she is the one runner whose profile genuinely suits several different pace shapes here.
runners_data.comment: Beaten into ninth last time out and unplaced the run before, Passing Thought heads into this carrying 131 lb from stall 1 rated 4 lb below her official mark on our figures, making her hard to fancy despite having run over today's trip and two wins in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Cotai Belle
runners_data.note: Relentlessly consistent placer whose six-run form string reads 822224, but she is a natural front-to-prominent type whose true position is being squeezed back by the more prominent horses in this field — the Fahey yard is in flying form but racing wider of her preferred spot will test her adaptability.
runners_data.comment: Cotai Belle has been a model of consistency, finishing second in four of her last six starts, and at 85 on our rating she shapes as a genuine threat from stall 2 off 126 lb; the risk is she remains yet to win despite every opportunity.

runners_data.name: Proposal
runners_data.note: Haggas's three-year-old won impressively at 7f on good and placed on Southwell's all-weather, showing she handles varying surfaces; she is at heart a horse that wants to race forward, and being pressed into a midfield role by the pace dynamics here means she will need to find an extra gear from a spot that doesn't suit her naturally.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Proposal faces a stiff task, and back-to-back fifth and fourth finishes in recent starts do little to inspire confidence; that said, she has winning form in her recent starts and has run over today's trip before.

races.paceDynamic: Oolong Poobong is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in this six-runner field, she is set to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop over Thirsk's 7f on good-to-soft ground. Passing Thought and Proposal both carry prominent tendencies but the field holds more pace-biased types than the map can accommodate — Cotai Belle and Proposal are true prominent racers who will likely be shuffled into midfield positions they do not naturally want, compromising their ability to race to their strengths. The most likely shape is therefore a moderately-run, uncontested lead for Oolong Poobong through the first half of the race, setting up a stern test from the two-furlong pole on soft-ish ground. This race shape strongly favours hold-up runners and genuine closers who can absorb the pace and finish through beaten horses late, with Figjam and Perfect Part the profile types built for exactly this scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Oolong Controls, Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Oolong Poobong dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the race develops into a genuine stamina test in the closing stages on good-to-soft ground.
scenarios.body: Oolong Poobong sets the fractions from the front while Figjam and Perfect Part stalk from the rear and unleash their finishing efforts in the final two furlongs; soft ground stretches the field and rewards those with the best late reserves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Passing Thought Front-Runs, Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Passing Thought pushes forward aggressively at the start and takes over or presses Oolong Poobong into a hot pace that backfires on the leader.
scenarios.body: With two pace angles in front the gallop increases materially and the race becomes a true test of stamina at 7f on soft, favouring a horse that can travel prominently and outstay rivals; Passing Thought's two wins on soft and good-to-soft mark her as a genuine candidate if she bounces into form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Caught Cold, Leader Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If Oolong Poobong steals an uncontested lead at a deceptively slow early pace and the hold-up brigade are too far back to close the gap.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race that never truly tests the front-runner allows Oolong Poobong to build a lead that proves insurmountable from the two-furlong mark; hold-up runners lack the early position to deliver their challenge in time on ground that does not promote rapid acceleration.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Disrupt Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Cotai Belle or Proposal force their way closer to the pace than their mapped positions suggest, creating a contested early gallop that scrambles the anticipated race shape.
scenarios.body: A more pressured pace would shorten the finishing straight battle and potentially benefit a prominent-travelling type who has conserved energy rather than a pure front-runner; however, because both Cotai Belle and Proposal are racing outside their natural position in this field, the scenario is inherently low-probability and its execution is uncertain.

watchPoints.text: Oolong Poobong's ability to control fractions unchallenged is the single biggest race-shape lever — if she gets a clean break and soft early sectionals, the hold-up runners face a genuine timing problem in the closing stages.

Passing Thought and Cotai Belle both carry forward-going tendencies, and any early jostling for position between them in the first furlong could inflate the pace beyond Oolong Poobong's comfort zone, dramatically changing the complexion of the race.

Proposal's 39-day absence combined with racing out of her natural position means she is a horse to monitor in-running rather than pre-race — Haggas runners can return fresh but the tactical compromise here is real.

Good-to-soft at Thirsk over 7f historically rewards horses with proven soft-ground form and genuine stamina; Perfect Part's placed run at 7f on soft is directly relevant, while Figjam's ten-length defeat last time on soft should be set against a weak-finishing effort rather than a ground concern.

The five-pound claimer on Cotai Belle (Ethan Tindall) and the three-pound claimer on Passing Thought (Ashley Lewis) are weight-saving factors worth tracking — in a low-key six-runner handicap, those allowances can be meaningful in a tight finish.

races.name: Rudding Park Harrogate Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Musical Touch
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for Fahey and Tindall (5lb claim), whose recent soft-ground record is poor — one run on similar going produced a 15th — and who hasn't raced for 42 days; needs a lot to go right from the rear in a race where the closers' path is compromised by the congested midfield.
runners_data.comment: Musical Touch won two starts back but was unplaced last time out, and 42 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has experience of today's trip and going, and his rating of 94 offers some encouragement, though he faces a stiff ask from stall 8 carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Grasmere Boy
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's lightly-raced 3yo has won twice at 6f on good ground and ran well at this trip last time; Jason Hart will want to sit second or third in Ray Mon Dough's slipstream, but four prominent rivals make clean air far from guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Grasmere Boy has run over today's trip and returns on a 28-day break, but back-to-back fifth-place finishes in his last two starts make him hard to fancy, and he ranks ninth of ten on our figures, leaving little reason to oppose that pessimistic read.

runners_data.name: The Good Biscuit
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's mare has won five times over 6f on good ground and her natural game is to race up with the pace — however, with four rivals also targeting that position, she is unlikely to land her preferred spot and will likely race a length or two further back than ideal, tempering her chance in this particular shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying a big 131 lb, The Good Biscuit also has a trainer badly out of form at 4% over the past fortnight — hard to fancy despite three wins in his last six starts and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Fivethousandtoone
runners_data.note: An 8yo veteran for Easterby and Allan whose genuine running style is to come from off the pace, but the volume of hold-up horses in this field means he'll occupy a midfield slot rather than the rearmost berth he prefers; soft-ground form is limited (0W0P in 2 runs) and he wears a hood.
runners_data.comment: Fivethousandtoone holds a clear edge at the top of the ratings and has run over today's trip and going before, but he arrives winless in his last six starts and his recent finishes of sixth and eighth give pause — second twice in that sequence, though, suggests ability is there.

runners_data.name: Midnight Thunder
runners_data.note: Suroor's 4yo won over this C&D at 6f on good ground and that form is obvious; Pierre-Louis Jamin takes the ride and the horse wears a tongue-tie — the concern is only one run on soft in seven starts, so his ability to handle today's ground needs proving.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Midnight Thunder nevertheless catches the eye rated 99 against an official mark of 92, and with experience of today's trip and going, he arrives in decent shape on a 20-day turnaround — the concern is that recent form has been too inconsistent to inspire full confidence.

runners_data.name: Commanche Falls
runners_data.note: A 9yo pattern-race type who races prominently and wears a hood; Michael Dods sends him out having placed in two of three recent runs on good, but he hasn't won in a long time and is yet to score on genuinely soft ground in 15 attempts.
runners_data.comment: Commanche Falls shaped with promise when third last time out, and his two seconds in recent starts highlight his consistency as a strong each-way threat; the concern is that he remains yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Dapper Valley
runners_data.note: Keady's 5yo is in excellent form with two recent wins at 5f-6f on good, and wears a hood; Michael Keady's yard has sent out no runners in the past fortnight, and while Dapper Valley typically races from off the pace, he has tactical adaptability and his recent momentum is a genuine positive.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom two on our figures and unplaced last time out, Dapper Valley is hard to fancy despite back-to-back wins two and three starts back; he has run over today's distance and going before, but 134 lb is a stiff ask for a horse rated this low in the field.

runners_data.name: Mostar Dreams
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's 5yo drops sharply from 7-8f on good ground to 6f on soft, and all five career runs in the form file are at 7f or 8f — the trip reduction is a significant unknown on top of a going question, and M.P. Sheehy takes the mount from Ireland.
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and a winner six starts back, Mostar Dreams has experience of today's trip and ground and returns after a 28-day break, though her latest ninth is a concern and she carries 142 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Dark Cloud Rising
runners_data.note: O'Meara's 4yo has strong recent 6f form — won once and placed twice from four runs at the trip on good — and wears a visor; Billy Garritty rides and the horse has only one run on soft in 15 career starts (unplaced), so the going is a legitimate concern that must be weighed against his otherwise solid profile.
runners_data.comment: Dark Cloud Rising brings strong recent form to the table — second and third earlier in the campaign — and has experience of today's distance and going; the sixth last time out is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Ray Mon Dough
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole's 3yo is the only genuine front-runner in the field and Kevin Stott can exploit that unchallenged lead on a flat 6f track; recent form includes a win at 6f on good and a second, and while soft-ground exposure is limited, his uncontested status is the defining tactical advantage in this race.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win two starts back before finishing eighth last time out, so Ray Mon Dough blows hot and cold, though he has run over today's trip and returns on a sharp 19-day turnaround carrying 137 lb from stall five.

races.paceDynamic: Ray Mon Dough is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Kevin Stott can dictate a controlled, honest gallop on good-to-soft ground without being pressured into overdoing it. Behind him, Grasmere Boy, Midnight Thunder, Commanche Falls, and Dark Cloud Rising all want to race prominently, creating a congested group of four chasing the same real estate between the 3f and 2f markers — traffic incidents in this pocket are a real danger. The Good Biscuit is a natural prominent type and Fivethousandtoone a natural hold-up horse; both are displaced by the volume of pace in this field and will not secure their preferred positions, meaning their redistribution to midfield is a concession rather than a tactical choice. On good-to-soft at Thirsk over 6f with a lone uncontested leader setting a sustainable tempo, this race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can track Ray Mon Dough in clean air and produce a one-two punch in the final furlong, rather than hold-up horses who must navigate through a congested midfield pack.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Ray Mon Dough dictates an uncontested, measured pace and the prominent chasers track cleanly in his wake.
scenarios.body: Ray Mon Dough sets a sustainable tempo on the good-to-soft surface, and the best of the prominent stalkers — ideally one who escapes the four-wide scrum — runs him down or presses past inside the final furlong. This is the dominant shape: a lone leader, soft ground that rewards those who conserve energy by sitting second or third, and no pace collapse to help closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Scrambles Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent runners fight for position 2-4f out, burning energy, and the cleanest traveller among them emerges while the leader fades.
scenarios.body: The congestion between Grasmere Boy, Midnight Thunder, Commanche Falls, and Dark Cloud Rising produces a messy middle sector, but the horse who finds the cleanest route — likely the one with most tactical speed — arrives at the 1f pole with enough left to reel in a tiring Ray Mon Dough. Soft ground amplifies the cost of the early barging, favouring the runner who threads through without losing rhythm.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Profit From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group burns each other out mid-race and the pace is genuinely strong enough to bring hold-up runners into play.
scenarios.body: A chaotic early scramble for prominent positions elevates the tempo beyond what soft ground can sustain, leaving gaps for horses coming from off the pace, though Mostar Dreams steps down sharply in trip from 8f and Dapper Valley has been in form; Musical Touch has a soft-ground concern based on recent history. This scenario is partially undermined by the fact that Fivethousandtoone, a redistributed hold-up type, is not in its natural position and The Good Biscuit is similarly displaced.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Leader Makes All Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If no prominent runner finds the energy or position to mount a sustained challenge and Ray Mon Dough simply gets away clean and stays there.
scenarios.body: On a flat track with soft ground, a fully uncontested Ray Mon Dough who is never headed could prove very hard to reel in if the chasing group wastes energy jostling, and Kevin Stott is adept at judging pace on this type of surface. This is a low-probability but genuine scenario if the prominent congestion behind him is more destructive than expected.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion — Grasmere Boy, Midnight Thunder, Commanche Falls, and Dark Cloud Rising will all seek to slot second or third behind Ray Mon Dough, making a physical battle for position between the 4f and 3f markers almost certain, with the horse that escapes cleanest likely to dominate the finish.

Dark Cloud Rising's going record — he has only one career start on soft ground from 15 runs and it produced a non-completion; if the surface is testing he may underperform his handicap mark despite good recent form.

Mostar Dreams' trip drop — all five runs in his recent form file are at 7f or 8f; dropping to 6f on soft ground with a jockey flying in from Ireland is a combination of unknowns that the market may not fully price.

Ray Mon Dough's lead exposure — if Kevin Stott is forced to go faster than he intends by any prominent rival getting on his shoulder early, the resulting stronger gallop would erode his stamina advantage and bring the hold-up horses into play more than the base scenario suggests.

The Good Biscuit and Fivethousandtoone will not race in their natural positions; backers of either should note their chance is partly contingent on benefiting from trouble in running rather than executing a clean tactical plan.

races.name: Calverts Carpets Hambleton Cup Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Acklam
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for Easterby with proven soft-ground form and a course-and-distance placed run in similar conditions, but her handicap mark has drifted to OR 80 and a wide draw in this field of mostly exposed horses makes a big finish from the rear harder to achieve.|
runners_data.comment: Spirit Of Acklam won two starts back and arrives here 26 days later in good order, with experience of both today's trip and going working in his favour; rated 96 and top of the eight, he has the class edge, though a return to form after his fourth last time is the one thing to prove.

runners_data.name: High Storm
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old returns after 99 days off, which with this trainer is not the red flag it might be elsewhere; he is mapped as a front-runner but the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that solo lead-stealing from a low draw needs verification — his soft-ground record (1 win, 2 places from 3) is the key positive.|
runners_data.comment: High Storm shaped as a strong contender on his official mark of 82 given our rating of 93, and he has experience of today's trip and going; the main concern is a 99-day absence, with only fourth and fifth in his last two starts to advertise his current form.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Myths
runners_data.note: Dr Newland and Insole saddle a lightly-raced three-year-old with a debut win and a third from just two runs; the 138-day absence is the main unknown, but a prominent racing style on a flat, potentially understandable track at 1m4f makes him a fascinating runner if fit.|
runners_data.comment: Bay Of Myths was a winner two starts back and ran a solid third last time out, giving him solid recent form to build on, though 138 days off the track is the key question mark he must answer fresh.

runners_data.name: What's The Plan
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's consistent hold-up horse has been placed in four of his last five, all at 1m2f on good ground; stepping up to 1m4f today is the key question, and soft ground at this longer trip is unproven — Harry Davies takes the ride with no apparent course angle.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in his last five starts, What's The Plan has been runner-up twice in recent outings and rates 5 lb above his official mark, making him a strong threat at the weights; the risk is whether he can finally convert.

runners_data.name: Kisiyra
runners_data.note: David Thompson's five-year-old has headgear on and has been placed twice at around 1m4f-1m5f, but his form on good-to-soft and softer is modest, and a 93-day absence combined with a conditional jockey booking (Ethan Tindall, 5lb claim) introduces uncertainty in a race where position matters.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Kisiyra has experience over today's trip but little recent form to recommend her, and a 93-day absence adds further doubt despite a handy weight of 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Wardlaw
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's progressive three-year-old has a cracking recent record — 1-2-2-3 — and stays 1m4f well; his natural last-to-first style is squeezed here because there are too many genuine closers, so he will likely be ridden more positively than ideal, which the STYLE_FIT tag reflects, though his class may compensate.|
runners_data.comment: Wardlaw won last time out and has run over today's trip, with a trainer firing at 35% over the past fortnight offering solid support; however, ranked sixth of eight on ratings and carrying 129 lb, he faces a stiff ask to confirm himself at the head of affairs.

runners_data.name: Knightsail
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's three-year-old is an authentic hold-up horse whose sole soft-ground run produced his only similar-going placed effort; repositioned into midfield on the map because the closers are oversubscribed, he faces the tricky task of finding room in a race that may not generate the searching pace he needs — 43 days off adds a minor fitness question.|
runners_data.comment: Knightsail shaped with promise when third three starts back, but has been below that level since, and winless in his last four outings; returning after 43 days off carrying 128 lb, he needs to find a gear here to threaten the principals.

runners_data.name: Mr Bollinger
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's lightly-weighted three-year-old has two wins at 1m4f on good ground and has form when fresh, so the 34-day break is not a concern; however, his natural last-to-first inclination is compromised by the clustered hold-up field, and his one soft-ground run at shorter (8f) produced an eighth — the going step up here is the clearest negative.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Mr Bollinger is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and a runner-up finish last time out; he has experience of today's distance and going, but a speed rating of 66 makes improvement to competitive level a tall order.

races.paceDynamic: High Storm is the one confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, he should be allowed to roll along at a measured, uncontested tempo over the 1m4f trip on Good to Soft ground. That controlled pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which means the horses sitting just off him in the prominent group — Bay Of Myths and Kisiyra — will travel comfortably without burning energy, while the genuine hold-up horses bunched in behind must hope the pace is strong enough to set up a meaningful late run. Wardlaw, Knightsail, and Mr Bollinger are authentic closers who have been mapped into midfield because the field contains more hold-up horses than can realistically operate from their preferred rear position; of the three, Wardlaw (with the strongest recent form) is most likely to find a position closer to the pace than usual, while Knightsail and Mr Bollinger may be forced wider or further back than ideal. This race shape — an uncontested, moderate gallop set by one front-runner on a flat, testing surface — strongly favours horses who travel prominently and conserve energy before hitting the front at the two-furlong pole, rather than those relying on a strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: High Storm Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If High Storm is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the pace remains honest but not suicidal, horses who track him prominently have every advantage.
scenarios.body: High Storm dictates a steady, sustainable gallop and the runners locked on his heels travel within themselves; as the tempo lifts entering the final two furlongs, Bay Of Myths and Kisiyra are ideally placed to pick him off or run him down.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the Good to Soft ground is more testing than expected and the prominent horses lack the finishing kick to reel High Storm in.
scenarios.body: High Storm, having been off 99 days but trained by K.R. Burke who regularly produces horses fit on return, builds a lead with energy in the tank and the soft ground blunts the finishing speed of those chasing; he simply keeps finding without being caught.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the final two furlongs become a genuine stamina test, giving the true closers a rare chance to close.
scenarios.body: Wardlaw, despite being nudged forward from his natural last-to-first role, has the best recent form in the field and could produce a powerful late run if the race develops into a slog; What's The Plan also stays well and would relish a genuinely run 1m4f on this surface.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If there is significant market drift in the main fancies and one of the lightly-exposed or unexposed types outperforms their handicap mark.
scenarios.body: Bay Of Myths, with only two career runs, remains a largely unexposed three-year-old who won on his debut and could be on a lenient opening mark; Mr Bollinger's win-and-place record at 12f on good ground gives him an outside chance if the pace scenario suits.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Bay Of Myths — who has raced just twice — is fully wound up after 138 days off; if he travels easily tracking High Storm in the early stages it is a strong signal he is fit and potentially well-handicapped on his opening mark.

High Storm's front-running role must be confirmed in the first furlong; if Bay Of Myths or Kisiyra push for the lead early, the pace will quicken and the race shape shifts significantly away from Scenario A.

Wardlaw's starting price and market movement is worth monitoring — Sir Mark Prescott rarely runs a three-year-old in this grade without confidence, and if the market shortens him, his compressed running style in this field should not be underestimated.

The Good to Soft ground at Thirsk today is consistent across all distances on the card, meaning no horse benefits from a false going report — stamina and soft-ground proven form should be taken at face value throughout.

Knightsail and Mr Bollinger are both genuine closers forced toward a midfield position; if neither can access the rail or a clear run in the final quarter-mile, their races may be run before the last two furlongs regardless of their ability.

races.name: Thirsk Racecourse Ideal Conference & Events Venue Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Kosometsuke
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form — including a 7f win on good — fits this trip well, but soft ground record is limited (3/14 sim-going, 1W1P); 81 days off is a concern, though trainer Michael Dods fields runners fresh; Connor Beasley knows the track and the hold-up profile means this one needs the pace to collapse.
runners_data.comment: Kosometsuke won four starts back but has since posted a fifth, eighth, and fourth in his last three, and at 81 days off the track he arrives short of recent match practice; he has run over today's trip and carries 137 lb from stall two.

runners_data.name: Misunderstood
runners_data.note: Placed twice on soft going at this trip and distance band, making her the standout soft-ground form reference in the field; David O'Meara's yard is firing (7/48 T14) and Jason Hart is an astute judge of pace; a genuine hold-up type who needs the tempo to sting.
runners_data.comment: Misunderstood has been knocking at the door, finishing second last time out after a string of near-misses, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions; carrying 135 lb from stall six is the chief concern for a gelding yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Andesite
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have come on good ground and the form figures on similar going are uninspiring (2/15, 0W0P); Roger Fell sends this one out on just two runners in 14 days and the switch to soft is untested — a going concern that undermines confidence at this level.
runners_data.comment: Andesite has been placed three times in his last six starts, including back-to-back seconds four and five starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the main risk is his last two outings have yielded only a fifth and seventh.

runners_data.name: Mythical Phoenix
runners_data.note: Prominent racer on paper but recent form shows a string of eighths and a 0 on the board in six starts, all on going faster than today; the soft conditions are unexplored and, though Julie Camacho's yard has been quiet (0/16 T14), this horse's style is the best fit for tracking Good Karma if the legs are there.
runners_data.comment: Mythical Phoenix has experience of today's trip and conditions, and our rating of 81 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark of 77 implies; winless in his last five starts, though, and that persistent lack of a finish is the concern.

runners_data.name: Frankies Dream
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up profile with all recent runs over 8f-10f on good ground, so dropping to 7f soft on a flat track represents a significant contextual shift; naturally suited to racing at the rear, this horse is shown in midfield only because the field is saturated with closers — in reality, expect a wide, held-up run and dependence on a strong pace that may not materialise.
runners_data.comment: Frankies Dream has been winless in his last six starts, though a third four starts back and a second five starts back hint at better days, and he arrives here on a fresher 28-day break having run over today's trip before; three consecutive finishes outside the top six make the turnaround he needs hard to envisage from stall 3 off 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Native Instinct
runners_data.note: Won on soft over 7f and placed twice on soft, giving the strongest like-for-like going credentials in the race; Edward Bethell's yard is active (3/22 T14) and the 17-day turnaround is not a concern; though a genuine hold-up type shuffled into a midfield slot by the congestion at the rear, this horse's soft-ground record means it retains genuine interest if any late pace develops.
runners_data.comment: Native Instinct won two starts back but has posted a fourth last time out and ranks eighth of nine on our figures, making him hard to fancy at the weights with 131 lb to carry, despite having experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ryley
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — note this at the time of race; if declared, this is a natural hold-up type with soft-ground form (7/6f/SOF, 1W2P sim-going) but all recent wins came over 6f, and the step up to 7f in this ground is a question; Alan Brown's yard has been quiet and the redistribution to midfield on the map reflects field congestion, not a change of plan.
runners_data.comment: Wreck It Ryley showed real promise with a third two starts back, and he returns on a sharp 15-day turnaround with experience of today's distance and going in his favour; yet to score in recent starts, but his rating of 82 makes him hard to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Intrusively
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer but all five recent runs have been on good or AW surfaces, and the form figures on similar going are poor (3/15, 0W0P); Michael Appleby's yard is active (3/25 T14) and Joanna Mason keeps the ride, but the absence of any soft evidence and the step back to 7f from recent 8f-10f runs makes this a speculative proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Intrusively at least has experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour, though a ninth last time out — 35 days ago — is hard to ignore, and carrying 127 lb from stall seven makes a significant step forward necessary.

runners_data.name: Native Honey
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good ground but all five recent runs produced only one placed effort and soft going is entirely unexplored; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is valuable but the horse is naturally a hold-up type shown in midfield due to field congestion — its real role will be at the rear, which needs a pace scenario that this race shape may simply not provide.
runners_data.comment: Native Honey is ranked ninth of nine on our figures, and consecutive fifths in his last two starts make him hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a reasonable 29-day break.

runners_data.name: Good Karma
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, and a 7f win on soft-ish (STA) gives some confidence that the conditions won't be prohibitive at OR=61; Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim helps with the weight burden, but the trainer has just one runner in 14 days and no obvious tactical firepower to change tactics mid-race — this horse will lead, and the question is whether the pace it sets is strong enough to stop the field closing.
runners_data.comment: Good Karma has managed just one win in his last six starts, and his speed rating of 59 leaves him well below the level needed here; ranked last on our figures, he is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip and going and faces a 19-day turnaround in reasonable freshness.

races.paceDynamic: Good Karma is the sole confirmed front-runner and, at OR=61, will stride out from the gates and aim to control proceedings from the front without any obvious challenger to press them into a genuinely strong gallop. On Good To Soft ground over 7f at Thirsk — a flat, fair track that does not inherently punish front-runners — a single pace-setter dictating at a controlled tempo creates a classic setup where those tracking close behind can travel sweetly without burning energy, making a prominent or close-tracking profile the most dangerous weapon. The hold-up brigade, which dominates this field numerically, will need Good Karma to fail and the pace to collapse late to deliver the ground they need, but with no genuine pace battle to sharpen the tempo that outcome is far from guaranteed. This race shape firmly favours horses able to race within two or three lengths of Good Karma through the middle stages and produce a sustained, rather than explosive, late challenge — the prominent/close-tracking profile is the clear beneficiary. Several runners are genuinely redistibuted here: Frankies Dream, Wreck It Ryley, Native Instinct, Intrusively and Native Honey are all natural hold-up types shown in midfield on the map, but with so many needing cover at the rear, they cannot all get their preferred position; the horses most likely to actually secure a prominent berth are Mythical Phoenix and whichever of the redistributed types can break sharply enough to pivot forward.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Good Karma Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Good Karma leads uncontested and the pace settles into a steady-moderate rhythm, allowing those tracking within two lengths to conserve energy.
scenarios.body: Good Karma sets a manageable tempo on soft ground, and horses that have tracked the leader prominently arrive at the 2f marker with enough in reserve to mount a sustained challenge rather than a sprint; the prominent racers and close trackers are perfectly placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Held-Up Types Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Good Karma goes too hard early and the soft ground extracts a toll in the final furlong, cracking the pace open for genuine closers.
scenarios.body: Good Karma, without the natural ability of a higher-rated horse, may overcook the pace trying to steal a march, leaving them vulnerable late as the ground bites; genuine hold-up horses who have raced well on soft previously could sweep through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Midrace
scenarios.trigger: If Good Karma fades abruptly before the 2f marker, turning the race into a sprint home from midfield.
scenarios.body: A soft-ground 7f with a lone exposed pace-setter can produce a sudden deceleration rather than a gradual fade, bunching the field and rewarding the horse with the freshest legs and best finishing kick; horses with recent soft-ground form and tactical versatility benefit most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate Finish
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types breaks sharply and secures an unplanned prominent position, racing into a slot that suits them better than their usual style.
scenarios.body: A horse like Native Instinct or Native Honey, breaking well and settling just off Good Karma's shoulder, could exploit the soft ground's premium on relaxed travelling and produce a strong sustained run; this scenario is discounted because it relies on horses racing out of their natural role with limited precedent at this trip.

watchPoints.text: Good Karma's early tempo is the single most important factor — watch whether Ethan Tindall elects to stride clear or ration energy; if Good Karma is allowed to coast, every hold-up horse in the field loses its only hope of a winning run-in.

Wreck It Ryley is listed as a non-runner — confirm declarations before betting as its removal reduces the number of runners and alters the pace dynamic marginally, though the overall shape remains the same with Good Karma still the sole leader.

With Frankies Dream, Intrusively, Native Honey and Native Instinct all naturally wanting cover at the rear, watch for a congested, wide finish in the final furlong as multiple hold-up types emerge simultaneously — this could compromise several of their chances through interference.

Native Instinct is the only horse in the field combining a soft-ground win over 7f with a placed record on similar going — if the pace does collapse late, watch this runner emerge from the pack as the most empirically-qualified closer in the race.

Misunderstood has placed three times on soft going across recent runs and arrives fresh off a 7-day turnaround for a trainer in form — watch whether Jason Hart opts to track closer than usual given the lack of pace pressure, which would markedly improve this horse's chance.

races.name: Thirsk Racecourse Ideal Conference & Events Venue Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Stanley Spencer
runners_data.note: Sole front runner with a clear lead mandate, but sim-going figures (1W in 15 soft-ground runs, 0W0P) are alarming for a horse being asked to front up on today's surface; racing beyond his typical 6f trip and T14 form of 0/2 adds further doubt despite the tactical advantage of an uncontested lead.
runners_data.comment: Stanley Spencer shaped with plenty of promise when second two starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going, combined with a rating of 85 that ranks him among the chief dangers, makes him a serious threat; the risk is that he comes into this yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Obelix
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up horse who has won over 7f on good ground and boasts solid recent form, but the ⚠ fade flag is a genuine worry on a soft surface that will amplify any tendency to idle or tire late; good-ground specialist (all five recent runs on good) stepping into soft today is the key concern.
runners_data.comment: Obelix posted a win five starts back and arrives here fit on 24 days' rest, with experience over today's trip and our rating placing him at the head of this nine-runner field; the worry is that he has managed just one victory in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Capital Guarantee
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for David O'Meara, whose T14 figures of 7/48 indicate yard is in reasonable nick; sim-going record of 2W in 15 runs on comparable ground is modest, and all five recent runs came on good — the step into soft is unproven but the prominent style suits the expected race shape.
runners_data.comment: Capital Guarantee won three starts back but has finished sixth in two outings since, suggesting he blows hot and cold; he has run over today's distance and going, carries 133 lb from stall eight, and 21 days between runs leaves fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Midnight Strike
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has shown ability over 7-8f and won on good ground; headgear (tp) noted, and the 34-day absence is among the longest in the field, though Jennie Candlish's T14 of 1/12 is acceptable; sim-going record of 8/15 runs in similar conditions with 0W2P suggests soft ground is not a barrier.
runners_data.comment: Midnight Strike shaped well when third last time out, and a winner three starts back, he arrives in decent nick after 34 days off with experience of today's trip and going to call on; the risk is that he has been in and out of form in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Mr King
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by history (hg:h), with a course-relevant 7f win on record and a ⚠ fade flag that could hurt in a race where closers already face a positional squeeze; 14 days since last run is sharp, and the 0W0P sim-going return in 3 comparable runs is a concern though the stamina profile fits a 7f soft-ground slog.
runners_data.comment: Winner three starts back, Mr King returns on a quick 14-day turnaround carrying 132 lb from stall one, with experience over today's trip an asset; the fifth last time out leaves something to prove, but he shaped well enough to hold interest at his best.

runners_data.name: Imperial Guard
runners_data.note: In strong recent form with three wins from his last four starts over 7f on good ground — comfortably the most in-form horse in the field; however, as a true hold-up type forced to operate from a midfield slot today, his ability to produce his characteristic late surge from the rear is compromised, and soft ground is untested (sim-going 1/15, 0W0P).
runners_data.comment: Imperial Guard has winning form in recent starts — a winner three runs back and two wins before that — but his unplaced effort last time out is an obvious concern, and ranked last on our figures he faces a stiff ask at 130 lb here despite having experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Packetofbiscuits
runners_data.note: Apprentice-ridden (Finlay Bassett, 7lb claim) hold-up type whose natural trailing position has been moved forward on the map to midfield; course-form over 7f at Standup and a second over 7f on soft (sim-going 1/15) show he handles similar conditions, but the positional compression means the 7lb claim may count for little if he cannot get a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Packetofbiscuits has struggled badly in recent starts, finishing eighth last time out and seventh the time before, and he ranks eighth of nine on our figures here, making him hard to fancy despite carrying a manageable 127 lb and having experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Fiscal Policy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent racer trained by Ruth Carr stepping up from 6f to 7f today — the extra furlong on soft ground is the primary question mark; yard's T14 figure of 1/26 is modest, and all recent form has been over 6f on good, but the prominent style naturally fits the expected race shape if stamina holds.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Fiscal Policy is hard to fancy despite a third last time out and experience over today's trip; the trainer's current 4% strike rate over the past 14 days adds little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Nyman
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's four-year-old, a genuine hold-up horse by inclination who is remapped to midfield given the surplus of closers; two wins and two places in his last 15 similar-going runs (2W2P) give the best sim-going return of any redistributed runner, and Joanna Mason's local knowledge is useful, but racing out of his preferred position limits his chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Nyman does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and returns on a reasonable 21-day break, but a ninth last time out is hard to ignore for a gelding carrying 125 lb from stall 3.

races.paceDynamic: Stanley Spencer is the sole confirmed front runner and, with Fiscal Policy and Capital Guarantee as the only other prominent types, the early gallop is likely to be controlled and measured rather than truly contested. On soft ground over 7f at Thirsk, a sustainable pace set by Stanley Spencer creates a race that stretches out steadily rather than explodes — the sectionals will compress late, rewarding those who can travel well through the race rather than those waiting for a sudden injection of speed. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Imperial Guard, Packetofbiscuits, and Nyman are genuine closers who will be shuffled into midfield positions rather than their natural berths, meaning their ability to produce a true late run from off the pace is compromised. This race shape — a lone, uncontested front runner on soft ground setting a steady gallop — classically favours prominent racers or those who can slot in behind the leader and get a clear, uninterrupted run, rather than the hold-up brigade who will be squeezed for daylight mid-race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Stanley Spencer dictates an uncontested, measured pace and the prominent racers track him into the straight.
scenarios.body: Stanley Spencer rolls along on soft ground at a pace that suits a sustained gallop, and horses who sit second or third travel comfortably before asserting from the 2f pole; the soft ground rewards those with genuine stamina who have not been asked early questions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Stanley Spencer settles into a rhythm so comfortable on the soft ground that the field cannot close him down.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to pressurise him, Stanley Spencer banks early energy and repels challengers deep into the 7f trip; soft going blunts the finishing kick of closers who never get into a meaningful rhythm behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Picks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough early to string the field out and create a gap for a late-running type to pick through.
scenarios.body: A horse from the midfield pack — where the redistributed hold-up types have been placed against their natural grain — finds a passage in the final furlong; this shape is less likely because Imperial Guard, Packetofbiscuits, and Nyman are not running from their true position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Soft-Ground Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground deteriorates sharply and the race turns into an attritional slog where stamina overrides tactics entirely.
scenarios.body: Tired rivals begin to stop in the testing conditions from 2f out, leaving the race wide open for any horse still finding a stride; this scenario depends on conditions being materially worse than the going report suggests and is the least predictable shape.

watchPoints.text: Stanley Spencer sets the early fractions unchallenged — if he gets away at a crawl on soft ground, prominent horses Capital Guarantee and Fiscal Policy must decide at once whether to push up and pressurise him or surrender the race shape entirely.

Imperial Guard's impressive recent winning sequence (three from four) makes him the form horse, but his true hold-up style is compromised by being mapped to midfield — watch whether Connor Beasley can find a clear passage in the final 2f or gets boxed in behind a tiring wall.

Obelix and Mr King both carry the ⚠ fade-in-finish flag, and soft ground at Thirsk over 7f will ruthlessly expose any tendency to idle — if either travels prominently into the straight they may empty sharply in the final furlong.

The going report confirms soft conditions consistent across all races today — any horse whose sim-going record is heavily tilted toward good ground (Capital Guarantee, Obelix, Midnight Strike) faces a genuine unknown that the form figures cannot fully account for.

Three apprentice or claiming jockeys are not represented here, but Finlay Bassett's 7lb claim on Packetofbiscuits is worth monitoring at the draw/early-position stage — a hold-up horse with a light weight could be vulnerable to a poor break that buries it even deeper than the redistributed midfield slot already implies.
